I have spent about eight years inside the paperwork of international trade —
first at a customs broker on the Blaine border crossing, then in export
licensing for aerospace, and now running import and export compliance for a
manufacturer and distributor in Bellingham.

The pattern across all of it is the same. The regulation is knowable. The
bottleneck is the data: thousands of line items, inconsistent vendor records,
classifications that were assigned once and never revisited. The wins I am
proudest of came from digging through entry data rather than from reading the
regulation more carefully.

I am finishing a B.S. in Data Analytics at Western Governors University to do
that work properly — SQL first, now Python. This site is where I practice on
public data.

## Where I have worked

**Import & Export Compliance Department Manager** — LFS Inc., Bellingham, WA
*(Mar 2026 – present)*

Own import and export compliance for a multi-million-dollar catalog. Build the
landed cost models that price 44 international suppliers, run restricted party
screening on outbound freight, and file all export declarations through AES
Direct. Recovered $500K in duties through an IEEPA trade data audit.

**Trade Compliance & Materials Specialist** — Korry Electronics, Everett, WA
*(May 2024 – Feb 2026)*

Drafted SNAP-R and DDTC export license applications and commodity jurisdiction
packages for aerospace defense articles. Ran ECCN classification and automated
screening in OCR EASE. Resolved an active trade embargo affecting Embraer
shipments through a root-cause classification audit.

**Logistics, Trade Data & Entry Specialist** — Pacific Customs Brokers / A&A /
TLR / UPS, Blaine, WA *(May 2016 – Mar 2024)*

Classified goods to 10-digit HTSUS across EPA, FDA, DOT, APHIS, and Lacey Act
requirements. Filed high-volume clearances in CargoWise, Editrade, and ACE.
Recovered $10M in duty refunds for corporate accounts under the Craft Beverage
Modernization and Tax Act.
